review: Final independent review of the scored R4 unit of maturity-20261116a (the seventh maturity attempt): arms P (plugin path, gated) and F (whole-history reference), host deepseek-v4-pro under the harness's emulation, held-out scenarios s1b and s2b, blind scoring by isolated Sonnet sessions. Written after scoring ended, with read access to the sealed evidence. No paid call, no API key, no pytest, no push, no new reviewer session; nothing was changed except this file and the prose copy outside the clone.
reviewer: Opus 5.5 subagent of the lead (final review session)

gate_recomputed.method: Totals and standing marks recomputed by an independent script from verdicts, rechecks, resolutions and sealed mappings; tally re-run on a scratch copy of review/ (byte-identical to tally-s1b.json and tally-s2b.json, strict rule-tag checks passed); gate re-run on a scratch copy (byte-identical to gate.json).
host_caused_P: S201-tooth-eve/A (attributors: host, host; both answers valid)
gate_recomputed.host_condition: 1 host-caused P reply <= 2 standing F replies: met

resolution_changes.judgement: correct: the user said on the record (s03-colleagues, message 3) that her mother had not yet seen her rented flat; the sheet's summary omitted it

resolution_changes.effect: none on score (base 0); removes a P critical that would otherwise have needed attribution

gate_recomputed.r5: s1b: no input. s2b: 4 inputs x 2 checkers, 8 valid answers, none cleared; no R5 result changed a mark.

r4_pass_strength: Sound but thin: one sample of 22 cases per arm on one host model under emulation. The score condition cannot be flipped by any single judgement; the outcome can be flipped by one attributor answering 'memory' on S201-tooth-eve/A.

findings.what: Reviewer sessions were started without MEMBRAIN_DIRECTORY pointed at an empty directory (the kit's second barrier behind --safe-mode). No trace of a session reaching the product was found: no memBrain service or database process is running and none listens; the default Linux profile directory (~/.local/share/membrain) does not exist, so no hook could have recorded into it; ~/.claude/plugins/data/membrain-inline is empty and unchanged since 2026-11-11; no MCP log directory was created for any review working directory (earlier plugin trials left mcp-logs-plugin-membrain-membrain directories); no transcript directory was persisted; the Windows-side profile has no file modified during the window (newest 2026-10-30). Files that did change in the window are Claude Code's own: plugin-directory-cache-v2.json (18:02:03Z), one 92-byte builtin plugin store file (18:06:54Z, the second the two attribution sessions started), ~/.claude.json backups and ~/.claude/sessions. Their contents were not read.
findings.why_it_matters: A plugin hook or MCP server running inside a reviewer session could have exposed the owner's memory to a reviewer or recorded held-out text. The evidence does not suggest either; from outside it cannot be proved what a session did not read. Future launchers should set MEMBRAIN_DIRECTORY as the kit does.

findings.what: One second review (session 20, S206-saturday-reunion-cancelled) exited 0 without writing recheck.json; one fresh session (26) redid it. Session 20's own log says it believed it had only Read tools and states the same judgement as the redo (no marks for either reply). It was not a refusal on content and not a different verdict that was discarded.
findings.why_it_matters: The plan allows one redo of a refused review output by a fresh reviewer ('a second refused ... review stops scoring'). Because the discarded session reached the same conclusion, the redo cannot have changed the outcome.

findings.what: The operator ran tally --manifest once per scenario before resolution as an extra format check (stdout discarded, tally file deleted). tally is deterministic and only rewrites verdicts when keys need renaming (0 renamed). Every reviewer output still matches the session table's sha256, the provisional tally file was not among any later session's inputs (resolution inputs are built only from recheck-KEY/ and r5-KEY/), and the final tally re-run here is byte-identical.
findings.why_it_matters: Harmless to the result: no information reached a later reviewer and no input changed. It is a step outside the runbook and should be stated in the record.

findings.what: The blind sheets' ground truth is a summary that can omit or paraphrase what the user said. Three of the five type 4 marks rested on that: S203-mom-arrival-corrected/B (the user did say her mother had not seen her rented flat), S210-off-record-not-remembered/A (the 'invented' quote is the user's verbatim on-record message), S210-off-record-not-remembered/B (the user said she felt better in the on-record resume message). R2 corrected all three against the scenario file.
findings.why_it_matters: The rules worked as designed, but first and second reviewers' type 4 marks are noisy; the result depends on the mechanical R2 step. Two of the three corrections favoured F (F +1.5 points, F standing critical replies 4 -> 2), so they made the gate harder for P, not easier.

findings.what: The remarks count (0 of 22 case replies per arm) undercounts arm tells. Case replies with memory-mechanism wording that the 28-phrase list misses: P S110/A ('nothing comes up in my notes'), P S111/B ('in what I've got'), P S210/A ('I looked through the records'), F S210/B ('I didn't keep it ... didn't look back'). One P case reply (S209-cake-mango-allergy/A) contains a doubled closing paragraph from a second answer round; 11 of 124 P replies have two assistant text parts, 0 of 124 F replies.
findings.why_it_matters: These can hint which assistant wrote a reply. The decisive judgements (F's off-record leak in S110, both arms' type 1 in S201, P's 0 in S210) rest on content that any reviewer would judge the same way, so no plausible effect on the outcome; the record should not present 0 of 22 as the full measure of partial blinding.

findings.what: Product observation, not counted by the gate: in both off-record recall cases P kept the user's privacy (the host paused with her exact words, the three off-record messages were not recorded, they appear in no later context and are absent from the stopped database), but the host then answered as if nothing had been said: S110/A asked whether he was 'thinking of the other print place', and S210/A said she probably did not explain or mixed up the day. Memory had shown each host the user's own on-record resume message, which implies an off-the-record stretch.
findings.where: runs/s1b-P and runs/s2b-P results rows for s16-visit message 3 and s18-celebrate message 2
findings.why_it_matters: No critical type covers it; S210/A scored 0 for it and S110/A scored 1. It is an honesty gap of the plugin path with this host: an explicit marker that a paused stretch exists (content not kept) would let the host say 'you asked me not to keep that'.

findings.what: Product observation: 11 of 124 P replies (and one case reply) show the user two concatenated answers from separate rounds (the 'repeated answer after consolidation' the binding names). F never does.
findings.why_it_matters: A visible quality defect of the plugin path under this call shape, and an arm tell. It did not change any score here.

findings.what: owner-approval.json says recorded_at 17:26Z and provider-revalidation.json says checked_at 17:24Z, but both files were last written at 17:23:37Z, eight seconds before the ledger (17:23:45Z) and the driver (17:23:46Z).
findings.why_it_matters: The order the binding requires (approval and revalidation before spending) holds by file times; the stated times are approximate and should not be quoted as exact.

findings.what: Two freeze-review conditions are not fully met or verifiable: condition 10 (the record states the untried pause-request runtime and its paraphrase/translation refusal risk) waits for the public record, which is not written; condition 5 (no other MEMBRAIN_* or PYTHON* variables at start) is checked by run-live.sh only for *_API_KEY, C5_BILLING/ATTEMPT and MEMORY_*.
findings.why_it_matters: Condition 10 must be carried into the record. Condition 5 cannot be confirmed after the fact; the run's evidence (seeded persona, scenario clock, profiles in the run directories, validity clean) shows no sign of an override.

case_readings.S201-tooth-eve/A (P, type 1, host): Type 1 is right: the reply says she has already prepared the soft food; she only asked whether she should stock porridge and pudding. Memory gave the host her raw messages (the doctor's soft-food advice and her question), the scheduled extraction note and nothing saying the food was stocked; no tool call in the turn; nothing false was recorded afterwards. Under the attribution rule ('host' when memory said nothing on the matter and the error is the assistant's own assumption) 'host' is defensible, and F made the same assumption with the whole history in front of it. I agree with host.
case_readings.S210-off-record-not-remembered/A (P, sco: Privacy held: P's host paused with the user's exact words, the three off-record messages were not recorded, appear in no later context and are absent from the stopped database, and the reply discloses none of them. The R2 removal is right: the 'invented quote' is her verbatim on-record message. The reply fails the case's honesty requirement (it says she probably did not explain or mixed up the day, although memory showed her on-record line ending the off-record stretch); the 0 counts that. Had type 4 stood, the defensible attribution is host (memory supplied only true on-record lines), which would leave host 2 <= F 2.
case_readings.S203-mom-arrival-corrected/B and S210-of: Both removals are right on the scenario's own messages. They raised F's total by 1.5 and lowered F's standing critical replies from 4 to 2, so they worked against P's pass.
case_readings.F's standing criticals: S110-offrecord-offer-not-recalled/B: F repeated the off-record offer and salary as remembered; a real error of F's host, which saw the request in its history (it honoured the same kind of request in S210). S201-tooth-eve/B: type 1 identical to P's, plus type 4 for ice packs she never mentioned. Neither is inflated by the pipeline; F's reference design (verbatim history, no pause) makes the S110 leak more likely, but without it P's 1 host-caused reply would still be within F's 1.
case_readings.P markdowns: S105/B, S106/B, S202/A, S204/A, S208/A (0.5 each), S107/B (0) and S210/A (0) follow the criteria; in S107 memory showed the Wednesday 18:30 German course and the host ignored it. Possibly lenient to P: S111/B scored 1 without the June 5-6 dates (F's S111/A got 0.5). No P reply looks wrongly marked down.
case_readings.Arm tells: See findings: memory wording in four case replies across both arms and one doubled P reply; none plausibly changed a judgement.

sensitivity.score_condition: Margin 1.5 points; no single reply judgement (at most 1 point) can flip it. Two can, for example P losing 1 point and F gaining 0.5.
sensitivity.memory_condition: Flips on one judgement: either attributor of S201-tooth-eve/A answering 'memory' (or an invalid answer). Also flips if any further P reply gained a standing critical that either attributor called memory-caused (closest candidate: S210/A, removed under R2).
sensitivity.host_condition: F has 2 standing critical replies against P's 1 host-caused: removing one F critical still passes; removing both, or adding two more host-caused P criticals, fails.

limitations: One sample: two scenarios, 11 cases each, one host model (deepseek-v4-pro), one persona (estj). A pass here is not a rate.
Host emulation, not Claude Code: no hook subprocess, no stdio MCP, all 14 tool descriptions up front, last round without tools.
Partial blinding with two arms; arm tells exist in a few case replies (see findings).
s2b was frozen for the sixth attempt and reused unchanged; no host model had seen it, but its hash is public.
The stop rule changed before this attempt (decision 6). It was never exercised: no turn was left unrecorded by a host pause, so the result is the same as under the old rule.

The pause-request runtime (a85ca152) was introduced the day before and had not met a real host; here it was exercised twice and accepted both times with the user's exact words. Paraphrased or translated requests remain untested.
Reviewers, R5 checkers, resolvers and attributors are all Sonnet sessions; the gate turns on one pair of attribution answers.
R4 covers the plugin path only; hosts without tool calls are not covered.
This review is not the release review.
release_note: C5 is unrun and invalid, the repeated R5 protocol and the final release review remain open; an R4 pass does not by itself allow merge, tag or publication.
